blocks.md:
Put **안** directly in front of the verb.

저는 커피를 **안** 마셔요. / I don’t drink coffee.

**하다 verbs split.** 공부하다 does not become 안 공부해요, the 안 goes **inside**, right before 하다:

공부**를 안 해요**  or  공부 **안 해요**  (○)
**안** 공부해요  (✗)

This catches everyone once. After that it feels natural, because 공부 is really a noun.

items.tip: I’m not going to school today.
I don’t work on weekends. Note the split in 일하다.

blocks.h: There is a longer form too
blocks.md:
**-지 않아요** means the same thing and sounds a little more formal or written.

안 마셔요  =  마시**지 않아요**

Learn to recognise it now; 안 is what you will actually say.

blocks.q: “I don’t exercise.”  (운동하다)
blocks.why: 하다 verbs split, so **안** sits right before 해요. 안 운동해요 puts it outside, which 하다 verbs refuse. 운동을 안이에요 mixes in the noun ending; the long form is written 운동하지 **않**아요, not 안아요.
**안** says you choose not to. **못** would say you are unable to, **잘** means “well”, **다** means “all”.

blocks.meaning: I’m not going to school today.
blocks.why: **안** says you are choosing not to go. **못** would say something is stopping you, **또** means “again”, **더** means “more”.

blocks.q: Which is the long form of 안 마셔요?
blocks.why: **-지 않아요** is the longer, slightly more formal twin of 안. 마시지 못해요 is the long form of **못**; 마시지 말아요 tells someone *not to* drink.

blocks.q: “I don’t work on weekends.”  주말에는 일 ___ 해요
blocks.why: 하다 verbs split, so 안 sits right before 해요.

blocks.q: Write it yourself: **“I don’t drink coffee.”**
blocks.hint: 안 goes directly in front of the verb, and the coffee is what you act on.
blocks.why: 저는 커피를 안 마셔요. Using 못 here would say you are *unable* to drink coffee, which is a different claim.

blocks.q: Say it out loud: “I’m not going to school today.”

blocks.md:
**못** goes in the same slot as 안, but means something different: **I am unable to.**

저는 수영을 **못** 해요. / I can’t swim.

Not a choice. A limit, no skill, no time, no permission, something in the way.

**못 splits in 하다 verbs too**, exactly like 안:

수영 **못 해요**  (○)  ·  **못** 수영해요  (✗)

items.tip: I’m busy today so I can’t go.
I still can’t speak Korean well.

blocks.md:
**-지 못해요** matches 못 the way -지 않아요 matches 안.

못 가요  =  가**지 못해요**

blocks.why: Spicy food defeating you is an inability → **못**. **안** would mean you simply choose not to, **잘** means “well”, **또** means “again”.

blocks.q: “I can’t swim.”  저는 수영을 ___ 해요
blocks.why: Not knowing how is an inability → 못.

blocks.q: “I can’t swim.”  (수영하다)
blocks.why: 못 splits 하다 verbs just like 안 does → 수영 **못** 해요. 못 수영해요 keeps it outside; 안 해요 says you choose not to; the long form is written 수영하지 **못**해요.

blocks.meaning: I’m busy today so I can’t go.
blocks.why: Being busy is a circumstance in your way → **못**. **안** would mean you decided not to, **잘** means “well”, **다** means “all”.

blocks.q: “I still can’t speak Korean well.”  한국어를 아직 잘 ___ 해요
blocks.why: Not being able yet is an inability → 못.

blocks.q: Write it yourself: **“I can’t eat spicy food.”**  (spicy food = 매운 음식)
blocks.hint: Your body refusing is not a choice, which of 안 / 못 is that?
blocks.why: 저는 매운 음식을 못 먹어요. 안 먹어요 would tell people you simply don’t care for spicy food.

blocks.q: Say it out loud: “I can’t eat spicy food.”

title.ko: Lesson 3. 안 or 못: will, or ability
title.en: Lesson 3. 안 or 못: will, or ability

blocks.md:
Now put them side by side. Same sentence, one word different, and you have said two very different things about yourself.

술을 **안** 마셔요. / I don’t drink. *(my choice)*
술을 **못** 마셔요. / I can’t drink. *(my body won’t let me)*

head: 안
못
rows: 못 먹어요: it makes me ill

blocks.md: **This matters socially.** Turning down food with 안 먹어요 says you did not want it. 못 먹어요 says you cannot have it. Koreans hear the difference immediately, and the second one is the polite way out of a dish you must refuse.

blocks.q: You are allergic to peanuts. Someone offers you some. What do you say?
blocks.why: An allergy is a limit, not a preference → **못**. 안 먹어요 would sound like you simply don’t care for them, 잘 먹어요 says you eat them well, and 다 먹어요 says you ate them all.

blocks.meaning: I’m busy today, so I can’t go.
blocks.why: Being busy is a circumstance stopping you → **못**. **안** would mean you decided not to go, **잘** means “well”, **더** means “more”.

blocks.meaning: I’m vegetarian, so I don’t eat meat.
blocks.why: Being vegetarian is a choice → **안**. **못** would suggest something prevents you, **아직** means “not yet”, **벌써** means “already”.

blocks.meaning: The tickets were sold out, so I couldn’t see the movie.
blocks.why: Sold-out tickets stopped you → **못**. **안** would mean you chose not to watch, **잘** means “well”, **또** means “again”.

blocks.q: A friend offers you a drink. You are driving. Which is right?
blocks.why: Driving takes the choice away from you → **못**. 안 마셔요 would sound like you simply don’t feel like it, 잘 마셔요 says you drink well, 다 마셔요 says you drank it all.

blocks.q: Write it yourself: **“I’m vegetarian, so I don’t eat meat.”**, just the second half: **“I don’t eat meat.”**  (meat = 고기)
blocks.hint: Being vegetarian is a decision you made, not something stopping you.
blocks.why: 고기를 안 먹어요. If you said 못 먹어요, people would assume an allergy or illness, and would worry rather than just cook something else.

blocks.q: Say it out loud: “I don’t eat meat.”

title.en: Lesson 4. Shaping Negations for Verbs and Adjectives

blocks.h: Where Negation Sits: Verbs vs. Adjectives
blocks.md:
How you negate depends on whether a word is an **action verb** or a **descriptive adjective**:

1. **Actions (동사):** Put **안** or **못** right before the verb. For -하다 action verbs, split them: **공부 안 해요 / 운동 못 해요**.
2. **Adjectives (형용사):** Use **안** only (never 못!). And do **not** split -하다 adjectives: **안 친절해요**, **안 따뜻해요**.
Why can't you use **못** with adjectives? Because **못** means *unable to do an action* due to ability or circumstance. An object cannot 'fail' at being small, warm, or pretty!

items.tip: The weather isn’t cold today. / Adjective 추워요 takes 안, never 못.
The room isn’t spacious. / Adjective 넓어요 takes 안.
I’m not doing homework now. / Action noun 숙제 splits with 안 해요.

blocks.q: Which sentence correctly says “The water is not hot” (뜨겁다 is an adjective)?
blocks.why: 뜨겁다 is an adjective (describes temperature), so it cannot use 못. Use **안 뜨거워요**.

blocks.q: How do you say “He is not kind” using 친절하다 (adjective)?
blocks.why: 친절하다 is a descriptive adjective, not an action verb. Adjectives do not split, so put 안 at the front: **안 친절해요**.

blocks.q: Match each phrase to its correct negative pattern.

blocks.meaning: These clothes are not expensive at all.
blocks.why: 비싸다 is an adjective describing price, so only **안** can negate it.

blocks.q: Make the polite negative form of 수영하다 (to swim) with 안: 「저는 바다에서 ___ .」
blocks.why: Action verbs with -하다 split so that 안 sits right before 해요: **수영 안 해요**. 안 수영해요 does not split the noun and verb, and 수영 하안 해요 is ungrammatical.

blocks.say: 이 가방은 전혀 안 무겁고 예뻐요.
blocks.rom: i ga-bang-eun jeon-hyeo an mu-geop-go ye-ppeo-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud: “This bag is not heavy at all and it’s pretty.”
Arrange the words to say: “I don’t exercise today.”
